summary.intent: Complete a GSD milestone management session for CipherBox project, discussing, planning, and executing phases 42 (API unpin integrity), 43 (FUSE write durability), and 44 (IPNS conflict handling) — three gap-closure phases identified during a UAT audit (PR #484).
summary.outcome: All three phases fully discussed, planned, and executed across wave-based parallel worktree execution. Phase 42 fully closed (8 plans, code review, verification, phase.complete). Phase 43 executed with 8 plans including a gap-closure wave, verified with UAT file for 4 runtime items needing human testing. Phase 44 executed 5 plans and code-reviewed; final close-out (phase.complete) not reached before transcript ends.

repo: Kubo runs with the `server` profile and swarm port 4001 exposed publicly (tcp+udp) in staging — it participates in the public DHT and broadcasts provider records for every pinned CID, making CIDs effectively public identifiers even though blobs are encrypted.

The `POST /ipfs/unpin` endpoint was behind `JwtAuthGuard` only — the handler never read `req.user`, passing the CID directly to Kubo `pin/rm`. Any JWT holder could destroy another user's pinned content by supplying a harvested CID.
Writable-share saves drop `prunedCids` without unpinning, meaning there was no legitimate cross-user unpin flow in the system — only the broken unguarded endpoint.

pnpm/jest passthrough gotcha: `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api test -- --testPathPattern=X` fails because pnpm inserts an extra `--`, causing jest to treat the flag as a positional test-name regex. Correct form: `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api exec jest --testPathPattern='X'`.
1Password SSH commit signing requires `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` on all `git commit` Bash calls; failures require user to restart the 1Password app — NEVER bypass with `--no-gpg-sign`.
The gsd commit helper returns `"committed": false` as a false negative even when the commit succeeded — always verify with `git log` and never blind-retry.
cleanup-wave must be run from the repository root; running it with cwd inside an agent worktree produces false `base_mismatch` errors because the helper resolves repoRoot from cwd.

cleanup-wave is not idempotent — it aborts the entire run on the first blocked entry; already-merged entries report `branch_mismatch` on rerun, so reduced manifests with only remaining entries must be written.

Phase 44 changed `updateFileMetadata`'s return shape from an IPNS record to `{ ipnsName, metadataCid, newSequenceNumber, prunedCids }`, removing the downstream `batchPublishIpnsRecords` call from callers.
BinEntry test fixture in sdk used `type` field where the actual type expected `itemType` — silently wrong until a plan's typecheck caught it.
sdk-core dist must be rebuilt before running typecheck on dependent packages (sdk, web) after changes to sdk-core source — stale dist causes spurious tsc errors.

code.finding: Upload-compensation path fired a global `pin/rm` on a content-addressed CID that may be shared with other users — no ownership check, same cross-tenant destruction vector as the main unpin endpoint. Fixed in plan 42-05 by routing through guardedUnpin.

Caller of `updateFileMetadata` that needed to be rewired to the new CAS contract (importing from `@cipherbox/sdk-core` instead of sdk, dropping redundant `replaceFileInFolder` call, adding `baseChildren` and `maxVersionsPerFile`).
Drops `prunedCids` without unpinning them — a pre-existing quota leak. Deferred as out-of-scope for phase 42; noted as a known debt item.

Kubo v0.40 configured with `server` profile and swarm port 4001 exposed publicly. The `server` profile only disables local-network discovery, not public DHT participation — all pinned CIDs are advertised to DHT crawlers.

Had a stray `spawn_journal.remove(&journal_entry_id)` call in the background upload thread — removing the journal entry on upload success before parent-pointer publish succeeded, creating an orphan window. Fixed inline after re-verification in phase 43 close-out.

workflow: The GSD worktree execution model (one git worktree per plan, isolated branches, wave-based parallel dispatch, manifest-tracked cleanup) works well for parallel safe execution but requires careful orchestrator hygiene: always run cleanup from repo root, never assume merge succeeded without checking git log, write reduced manifests on partial retries.

When a planner agent dies mid-run (socket close after writing 3/8 plans), the correct recovery is to verify which plan files exist and are complete on disk, then spawn a continuation planner for the remaining plans — avoids re-planning already-complete work.

Decision coverage gates use mechanical grep for literal `D-NN:` citations — plans must include explicit citation lines in `must_haves` sections for decisions they implement, not just implement them implicitly.
prettier mangling .planning markdown is caused by no `.prettierignore` — creating one early in a project prevents planning artifact corruption in pre-commit hooks.

For the concurrent unpin dedup race: per-CID advisory lock (`pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(cid))`) around the delete+refcount+outbox insert closes the race transactionally — a drift report job is detect-only defense-in-depth, not the primary fix.

Code review findings from gsd-code-reviewer are advisory and must not block phase close-out; the execute-phase workflow explicitly requires proceeding to verify_phase_goal regardless of review status.

friction: 1Password SSH signing failures required user to restart the 1Password app mid-session; each signing attempt that fails blocks the entire commit flow until recovery.
gsd commit helper false negatives (`"committed": false` while commit landed) caused wasted retry attempts and required a `git log` verification step after every commit.
Session quota limits were hit twice, forcing work to be resumed across context boundaries and requiring re-dispatch of already-running background executors.
User accidental inputs ('touring wyatt web bossy') interrupted the execution loop twice, requiring pause-and-resume cycles.

cleanup-wave aborts entirely on the first blocked worktree entry and is not idempotent — repeated merge attempts require manually constructing reduced manifest files with only the not-yet-merged entries.
Worktree merge blocked by untracked `node_modules` and `.husky/_` directories left by executor agents — required manual cleanup before cleanup-wave could proceed.
42-05 merge left a `MERGE_HEAD` state (all conflicts auto-resolved, but commit step failed silently) requiring manual `git commit --no-edit` intervention.
openapi.json formatting drift from `nest build` side effects polluted the working tree during wave merges, requiring `git checkout --` restore before each merge.
Post-merge typecheck failures for sdk and web after phase 44 wave 3 were caused by stale sdk-core dist — required an explicit `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk-core build` rebuild step.
No `.prettierignore` existed at project start, causing prettier to mangle planning docs and break test command regexes in VALIDATION.md tables (pipe characters interpreted as markdown table columns).
Planner agent died with a socket error after writing 3 of 8 plans for phase 42, requiring a filesystem fallback check and continuation planner spawn.

Phase 43 has 4 runtime UAT items requiring human verification (mount-and-write crash recovery, WinFsp cross-compilation, macOS FUSE notification, WriteParked tray notification) — documented in 43-UAT.md.
Phase 44 final close-out not completed: phase.complete, todo closure, PROJECT.md update, and ROADMAP completion annotation still pending.
Deferred: pending-uploads UI — user requested this be noted as a future improvement during phase 43 discuss (full pending-uploads panel with status counts).
Deferred: BYO provider.unpin client wiring — the server-side fix handles BYO correctly but the SDK/FUSE client side never calls provider.unpin on delete.
Deferred: writable-share `prunedCids` leak at `shared-write.ts:450` — versions are pruned from metadata but the CIDs are never unpinned, leaking quota.
Deferred: Rust FUSE three-way merge parity for IPNS conflict handling (phase 44 D-09) — conflict handling is TypeScript-only in this phase; Rust crates/fuse remains unaddressed.
